material.report:
--- final reply ---
# Reservation flow review: Fernhill Tool Library

I reviewed all five pages (find → tool → basket → confirm → done) and `app.js`/`styles.css`, using the two journeys in `journeys/` and the facts in `PRODUCT.md`. I measured the dark-mode contrast numerically. **I did not run the pages in a browser or on a phone, and I did not test them with a screen reader.** Each finding below comes from reading the code. Where I worked out what a 375 px phone would show, I say so. I didn't change any files.

## Fix these before launch

### 1. Members can reserve a day the library is closed, or before the tool is back, and only find out at the last step
- On the tool page you can pick any of the next 21 days. Nothing stops you choosing a day without a session (`app.js:195-208`). The member learns this only after filling in their details and tapping **Confirm reservation**. After a 1.5 s wait they get "The library is closed on … Choose another day" (`app.js:421-430`). That error has no link and no way to change the day. The basket doesn't let you edit the day either, so the only way out is to remove the tool and start again.
- Days before the tool's "Available from" date aren't blocked. Take the pressure washer, which is available from 17 Oct. You can reserve it for Saturday 10 Oct and the reservation **succeeds**, because the 10th is a session. The desk ends up with a reservation for a tool it doesn't have. That breaks your "honest about the stock" commitment.
- **The member picks a date twice, and the two can disagree.** They choose a pick-up day on the tool page and then a session in the basket. Nothing links the two. In the "change pickup session" journey, the confirm page ends up saying *"Cordless drill … pick up Saturday 17 October"* right above *"Pick-up session: Wednesday 21 October"*. The closed-day check also looks at the tool page's day, not the session the member actually chose.

**Fix:** have the member choose the date in one place only. My recommendation is to drop the free calendar on the tool page and let them choose from the session list. Only offer sessions on or after the tool's available-from date (the latest date across everything in the basket), and use that one choice everywhere. If you keep the calendar, make the non-session days and the days before the tool is available unselectable (`disabled`, and leave them out of the tab order).

### 2. The basket hold expires silently and then blocks the member for the rest of the visit
- The hold is ten minutes from the first tool added (`HOLD_MINUTES`). The basket page only says "Items are held for you while you finish". It never mentions a time limit, shows a countdown or offers a way to extend it. WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing adjustable) requires some way to turn off, adjust or extend a time limit like this, with a warning before it runs out.
- When the hold runs out, **Continue** shows only "Something went wrong. Try again." (`app.js:360-364`). Trying again never works, because the hold start time is only cleared by "Reserve another tool" on the done page. Removing the tools and adding them again doesn't clear it either. **The member can't finish a reservation in that tab at all.**
- Your main user is on a phone in the evening, "doing something else", with "a cup of tea going cold". Going past ten minutes is a normal case for them.

**Fix:** state the limit when the first tool is added ("We'll hold this for 10 minutes"). Warn near the end and offer to extend. When the hold has expired, say so in plain words and re-hold the tools if they are still free. Reset the timer whenever the basket becomes empty.

### 3. On a phone the two drills look identical, and search and filters sit below the whole list
- Tool names are cut to one line with an ellipsis (`styles.css:372-381`). At 375 px a card leaves roughly 200 px for the name. By my estimate, both "Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries" and "… one battery" show as about **"Cordless drill 18 V, co…"**. That is exactly the difference the main journey depends on, and larger text makes it worse. **Fix:** let names wrap.
- At 480 px and below the results come *before* the search form (`styles.css:261-269`). A member looking for "drill" has to scroll past all ten cards to reach Search. The "Available from" filter (top task 3) sits behind an icon-only button below that. **Fix:** put search first on phones, and show the date filter instead of hiding it.
- On desktop the reverse happens. The form is shown first, but its code still comes after the results, so keyboard and screen-reader order doesn't match what members see (WCAG 1.3.2 and 2.4.3).
- The results grid has a minimum column width of 330 px. At 320 px wide, or at high zoom, the page scrolls sideways (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow). Use `minmax(min(330px, 100%), 1fr)`.

### 4. A search with no results leaves the old list on screen
`search()` only redraws when it finds something (`app.js:158-164`). Search for "hammer" or "drll" and the previous list stays put. There's no "No tools match" message, and screen readers hear nothing. Members will think the old list is their result. **Fix:** always redraw, and show an empty state such as "No tools match 'hammer'. Clear search", plus the desk number.

### 5. Double-tapping Confirm makes two reservations
Confirm creates the reservation number straight away and then waits 1.5 s (`app.js:413-433`). The button is never disabled, and nothing on screen shows that it's working: `aria-busy` has no styling. On a slow phone a second tap creates a second reservation, and the done page then shows "Reservation numbers FT-4471 and FT-4472". The desk sets the tool aside twice. The Continue button in the basket has the same missing busy state.

**Fix:** disable the button on submit, show "Confirming…", and ignore repeat taps.

## Fix next

6. **Dark mode: the green "Available from" badge is hard to read.** In dark mode `--color-ok` is `#2f7d4a` on `#1d2622`. That's **3.07:1**, and 16 px bold text needs 4.5:1. `DESIGN.md` specifies `#8fd1a8` for dark success (about 8.8:1), so the CSS doesn't follow the design. The badge background is also the same colour as the card, so it doesn't look like a badge. This is the only text that failed in my dark-mode contrast check. Body text, links, buttons, errors, the focus ring and the "Open" dot all passed.
7. **The loan-length dropdown is hard to use by keyboard and confusing with a screen reader.** Once it's open, Tab and Shift+Tab only cycle through the options, Escape doesn't close it, and tapping outside doesn't close it either (`app.js:238-251`). The button's accessible name is just "One week", without "Loan length". **Fix:** there are only two options, so use two radio buttons, or a native `<select>`.
8. **The "Added to your basket" message disappears after about 1.2 s, and the member isn't told what to do next.** Many members are older, so this is too fast. After reserving, the only way forward is the small "Basket (1)" link in the header. **Fix:** keep the message on screen with a "Go to basket" link. Better still, change the bar's button to "Go to basket" once the tool is added.
9. **Sessions in the basket are shown in reverse order.** The `row-reverse` and `wrap-reverse` styles (`styles.css:816-822`) put Wed 28 Oct at the top on a phone. Screen readers and keyboard users get them earliest first. **Fix:** remove the reversal so they're shown in date order.
10. **The membership and phone checks are too strict.** "ft-01234" and "FT 01234" are rejected; phone keyboards often lower-case the first letter. "+44 7700 900123" and "07700 900 123" are rejected too. **Fix:** accept these and tidy them up before checking. Use `autocapitalize="characters"` on the membership field.
11. **Only the "Open" label shows which days are sessions on a phone.** Below 480 px it becomes an unlabelled 8 px dot. Screen readers do hear "open". This stops mattering if you fix item 1.

## Smaller issues
- The done page shows a made-up reservation number, "FT-4471", if it's opened without reservation data (`app.js:443`). Reservation numbers also look like membership numbers ("FT-…"); use a different prefix.
- After confirming, the basket still holds the tools unless the member taps "Reserve another tool". Members could easily reserve the same tool again. Empty the basket once the reservation is confirmed.
- The page doesn't enforce the "up to three tools" limit.
- The fixed Reserve bar on the tool page covers the footer, which has the desk phone number, at the bottom of the page. Add bottom padding equal to the bar's height.
- When Reserve is tapped without a day, the error "Choose a pick-up day first" isn't read out. Focus moves to the first day button instead. Link the error to the calendar, or announce it.
- Headings: tool names on cards are `h2` inside the "Tools" `h2`; make them `h3`. On the done page, the hidden `#c-tool` makes screen readers read the tool name twice.

## Suggested order
1. Make the date a single choice that only offers real sessions on or after the tool's available date (item 1).
2. Make the hold visible, extendable and recoverable (item 2).
3. Let tool names wrap, and put search first on phones (item 3).
4. Fix the empty search result and stop double reservations (items 4 and 5).
5. Fix the dark-mode badge colour, the loan-length control, the "added" message and the session order (items 6–9).

Items 1, 2 and 5 can create wrong or duplicate reservations at the desk, or lock members out, so they need fixing before members get access. Items 3 and 4 slow down the main phone journey. Once items 1–5 are fixed, I'd run both journeys on a real phone in dark mode, with VoiceOver and at 200% text size. That check is still to do; this review didn't include it.

I reviewed the whole reservation flow by reading the five pages, the script and the stylesheet. I also checked dark-mode colour contrast numerically. I didn't open the site in a browser or on a phone, or try it with a screen reader, so what follows comes from the code. I haven't changed any files.

**Fix these before launch:**

1. **The pick-up date can be wrong or contradictory.**
   - The calendar on the tool page lets a member pick any day, including days the library is closed. They only find out after entering their details and pressing Confirm, and that error gives them no way to change the day.
   - Days before a tool is back aren't blocked. A member can reserve the pressure washer (available from 17 Oct) for Saturday 10 Oct, and it goes through, so the desk gets a reservation for a tool it doesn't have.
   - Members choose a date twice, a day on the tool page and a session in the basket, and nothing keeps the two the same. The confirm page can say "pick up Saturday 17 October" right above "Wednesday 21 October".
   - **Fix:** ask for the date once, from a list that only offers real sessions on or after the tool's available date.
2. **The 10-minute basket hold can lock members out.** Nothing tells them there's a time limit, and they can't extend it. When it runs out, Continue just says "Something went wrong. Try again." Trying again never works, even after emptying the basket, so the member can't finish in that tab. Your evening phone users will often take longer than ten minutes. **Fix:** say there's a limit, warn before it ends and let members extend it.
3. **On a phone, the two drills look the same.** Tool names are cut to one line, so both drills should show as about "Cordless drill 18 V, co…". Search and filters also sit below the full list of tools on phones. On very narrow screens or at high zoom, the page scrolls sideways.
4. **A search with no matches leaves the old list on screen**, with no "nothing found" message, so it looks like a result.
5. **Double-tapping Confirm makes two reservations.** The button stays active and shows no sign that it's working.

**Fix next:**

6. **Dark mode:** the green "Available from" label fails contrast (3.07:1 against the 4.5:1 minimum). The stylesheet uses a darker green than your design document specifies. It was the only text that failed my dark-mode check.
7. **Loan-length dropdown:** with a keyboard, Tab only cycles through the two options and Escape doesn't close it. Screen readers hear "One week" without "Loan length". Two radio buttons would be simpler.
8. **"Added to your basket" message:** it disappears after about a second and gives no "Go to basket" link.
9. **Session order:** the basket lists sessions latest first on screen, but screen readers and keyboards go through them earliest first.
10. **Form checks are too strict:** "ft-01234" and "+44 7700 900123" are rejected.

The full write-up, with line references and a list of smaller issues, is in `.eval/reply.md`. Once items 1, 2 and 5 are fixed, I'd run both journeys on a real phone in dark mode, with VoiceOver on and at 200% text size.

ground_truth.description: At 480 px and below the stylesheet reorders the page so the list of tools comes before the search form, and the only way to the 'Available from' date and the category filter is an icon-only button (three lines) that opens a collapsed panel below the list. A member who wants tools for a given Saturday sees ten cards first and no date control, so they are unlikely to notice that filtering by day exists. The document order is form then results, so keyboard focus also runs against the visual order.

A search with no matching tool (for example 'sewing machine') leaves the previous results on the page and shows no message: the status region stays empty and the list does not change. The member cannot tell whether the search ran, whether nothing matched, or whether the old list is the answer.

Tool names are kept on one line and cut with an ellipsis inside the card's text column. At phone widths 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, one battery' both read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…' (at 375 px; a character more or less at other widths), so a member cannot tell which card is the right one without opening each; only from about 480 px does the difference show. The full name is only in the link's hidden overflow.

In the dark theme the 'Available from' badge is a mid green (#2f7d4a) on the card surface (#1d2622), about 3.1:1 for 16 px bold text, below the 4.5:1 that text of that size needs; the light theme passes. Members who use dark mode on their phones get the availability line as the least legible text on the page.

The results grid asks for columns at least 330 px wide; at 320 px the content box is 288 px, so the cards run 42 px past it and the page scrolls sideways by 26 px. The same happens at 200% zoom on a 640 px window.

Every day in the calendar can be chosen, including the days the library is closed; only session days carry the word 'Open' (a green dot on a phone). Choosing a closed day highlights it and the page confirms 'Pick-up day: Monday 12 October'. The reservation is refused three steps later, on the confirm page ('The library is closed on Monday 12 October…'), and the only way back to the calendar is the browser.

Pressing 'Reserve this tool' shows 'Added to your basket' for 1.2 seconds and nothing else changes nearby; the only lasting sign is the basket count in the header, which on a phone is above the fold. A member who looked away, or who reads slowly, does not know whether the press worked and presses again.

The 'Reserve this tool' bar is fixed to the bottom of the window and nothing keeps the page clear of it: the page ends 8 px under the calendar and the footer runs under the bar. A day button that sits in the bottom 72 px of the window counts as visible to the browser, so Tab reaches it without scrolling and the bar covers the focused control: at 768 px wide (900 px tall) the first two rows of days, at 1280 px the third row; on a phone the footer and the desk phone number sit under the bar at the end of the page.

The loan-length list opens as a custom listbox. Inside it, Tab moves to the next option and wraps around, and Escape does nothing, so a keyboard user cannot leave the list except by choosing an option with Enter.

The basket says 'Items are held for you while you finish' but shows no time; the hold is ten minutes from the first item and is kept only in the browser. When it has lapsed, Continue waits 1.2 seconds and then says 'Something went wrong. Try again.', which is not what happened and does not say what to do.

The pick-up sessions are laid out in reverse (row-reverse with reversed wrapping), so the earliest session appears last on screen, at the bottom of the stack on a phone and at the end of the row on a desktop, while coming first in the document. Tab moves from the rightmost card leftwards, against reading order, and a screen reader hears the sessions in an order a sighted member does not see.

'Confirm reservation' stays enabled while the request runs for 1.5 seconds, and nothing visible says that anything is happening. A second press, which is what people do when nothing seems to happen, allocates a second reservation number; the confirmation page then lists two reservations for one visit, and the desk holds the tool twice.

The 'Change' link beside the pick-up session returns to the basket without the chosen session, so a member who only wanted to look at the summary comes back to a basket with no session selected and has to choose again. Nothing says the choice was dropped.

The calendar neither marks nor disables the days before the tool's 'Available from' date, the basket offers every session, and confirm does not check: a wet tile saw available from Saturday 24 October reserved for Saturday 10 October ends on 'Reservation confirmed'. The member is told a tool will be waiting when it cannot be, and finds out at the desk.

Each tool keeps the pick-up day chosen on its tool page, the session is chosen separately in the basket, and nothing reconciles them: a drill to be picked up on Saturday 17 October can be confirmed for the Wednesday 21 session, the confirm page shows both dates and the done page only the session, so it is unclear which day the desk sets the tool aside for.

The loan-length button has no aria-label or aria-labelledby, so its accessible name is only its current value: a screen-reader user hears 'One week, button, collapsed' and is not told what is being chosen.

The membership number must match /^FT-\d{5}$/ and the mobile number /^0\d{4}\s?\d{6}$/, with no normalising: 'ft-01234', 'Ft-01234' (what a phone's sentence capitalisation makes of it) and 'FT 01234' are rejected, and so are '07700 900 123' and '+44 7700 900123', the form phone autofill often supplies. Each gets an error whose example looks like what the member typed.

After 'Reservation confirmed' the basket is not emptied: the header still reads 'Basket (1)' and the basket still lists the tool as held, and going back to the confirm page and confirming again reserves the same tool a second time under a new number.

Pressing 'Reserve this tool' with no day chosen shows 'Choose a pick-up day first.' in a paragraph with no role or live region that the calendar does not reference, so it is not announced, and focus moves to the first day button, a closed day before the tool is available. The message stays on screen after a day is chosen.

Below 480 px the word 'Open' on session days is hidden and an 8 px dot takes its place; what the dot means is only in the hint above the calendar. On the phone, the members' main device, which days the library opens is easy to miss. The seeder chose the dot to fit the calendar at phone widths; the second labeller and two reviews judged it a minor problem.

The find page says members may reserve up to three tools at a time, but the basket takes a fourth tool without a warning and the reservation is confirmed for four, so the desk has to turn the member away from some of them at collection.

With the membership number, name and mobile filled in, 'Change', the basket and Continue bring the member back to the confirm page with all three fields empty; the details are kept nowhere, so she types them again on a phone.

The tool page asked for a pick-up day and the basket line repeats it, yet no pick-up session is selected and Continue answers 'Choose a pick-up session', so the member enters the same date a second time, in another form, and can choose a different one.

On the done page the Tools entry holds the visible list item and a visually hidden span with the same name, so screen readers read the reserved tool's name twice; next to two reservation numbers this can sound like two tools.

The 'Available from' filter keeps the tools that can be collected on the chosen day, but its label uses the badges' words and its hint says 'Show tools you could pick up on or after this day': choosing 14 October hides a tool available from 17 October, which could be picked up after the 14th.

'Reserve this tool' does not reserve: it puts the tool in a basket held for ten minutes, the button keeps its label, and nothing says that a basket, a session and a confirmation still follow. A first-time member can believe the tool is reserved and put the phone down, and the hold lapses with nothing reserved. It is the press D07 describes, read for a different harm: D07 is the brief feedback, this is the misleading action.
